task_packet.title: Diagnose missing subclass data in nested union serialization
task_packet.issue_text: Reported with Pydantic 2.9.2, pydantic-core 2.23.4, and Python 3.10.4. A nested model field is annotated ParentClass | ChildClass. ParentClass is an empty BaseModel; ChildClass inherits from it and defines field1: str and field2: float = -5. Construct the nested model with ChildClass(field1="world") and call model_dump(mode="python"). The report says the nested output omits field1; changing the default from -5 to -5.0 avoids the reported behavior. No repository checkout, code execution, or browsing is available. Using only this report and the supplied context, explain a plausible diagnosis, recommend a focused investigation/change direction, and outline regression tests. Separate observations from hypotheses; do not claim reproduction or a confirmed root cause.

source.title: Cached property erroneously included in model export

task_packet.title: Diagnose cached-property data appearing in model export after assignment
task_packet.issue_text: Reported with Pydantic 2.6.4, pydantic-core 2.16.3, and Python 3.11.7. A model configured with extra="allow" and validate_assignment=True has a declared name: str field and an undecorated functools.cached_property named extra_info. The report says model_dump() contains only name before and after reading extra_info, but includes extra_info after assigning a new name. No repository checkout, code execution, or browsing is available. Using only this report and the supplied context, explain a plausible diagnosis, recommend a focused investigation/change direction, and outline regression tests. Separate observations from hypotheses; do not claim reproduction or a confirmed root cause.
acceptance_criteria: State the observed before/after serialization behavior without generalizing beyond the reported case.
Use the supplied documentation context carefully and distinguish documented behavior from an unverified historical issue-version expectation.
Propose tests around property access, assignment, model_dump(), and model_dump_json().
Give a narrow change/invariant to investigate and identify uncertainty or compatibility risks.
